🌱 It's Doing a Bit

A genuine nought for two — both openers gone and not a single run, not even an extra, on the board when the second wicket fell, and both to the bowling (a run-out doesn't count — the pitch has to be to blame). The purest evidence the surface, or the new-ball pair, meant business — and rarer than you'd think.

🚑 Man Down

The over nobody could finish. In cricket you can only hand over mid-over if you leave the field, so these are the spells cut short by a tweaked hamstring or a rolled ankle — the bowler helped from the attack and a team-mate sent to mop up the rest. (A won run-chase ends the innings cleanly, so those never count.)

🧐 Where Are the Drops?

Cricket's cruellest secret: Play-Cricket scorecards don't record dropped catches, misfields or fumbles — only what actually got a batsman out. So the fielding dishonours can only be the keeper's byes above. The day shelled chances get logged, this is where they'll live.
